entries.name: Woodland BDU
entries.summary: Four-color woodland camouflage battle dress uniform. The Army field uniform from the early 1980s until the ACU.
facts: Adopted in 1981 as the Battle Dress Uniform (BDU)
Replaced by the ACU, fielded starting in 2005
A six-color desert version was issued for desert operations

variants.label: Woodland BDU (four-color)
variants.note: The standard green, brown, and black pattern.

entries.name: Pinks and greens
entries.summary: WWII-era officer service uniform: pink-toned trousers with a dark green coat. Brought back in modern form as the Army Green Service Uniform.
facts: Pink-toned trousers with a dark olive-green coat
Officer combination in World War II
The modern Army Green Service Uniform revives the look
entries.remember: Pinks on the legs, greens on the coat.

variants.label: Army Green Service Uniform
variants.note: The modern revival of the look.

entries.name: Army Blue dress uniform
entries.summary: Dark blue formal uniform worn for formal and ceremonial occasions.
facts: Service stripes and overseas service bars go on the sleeves
Ribbons and badges go above the left pocket
entries.remember: Blue is for dress, green is for service.

entries.name: Sharpshooter badge
entries.summary: Middle marksmanship qualification badge, above Marksman and below Expert. Weapon bars hang underneath.
facts: Three levels: Marksman, Sharpshooter, Expert
A bar for each weapon type hangs from the badge
Comes in a polished (shiny) finish and a subdued (non-shiny) finish

attachments.name: Qualification bars
attachments.note: Bar names and the full bar list still need to be checked.

entries.name: Parachutist badge
entries.summary: Army jump badge in three levels: Basic, Senior, and Master.
facts: Three levels: Basic, Senior, Master
Combat jump stars mark combat jumps
entries.remember: Basic, Senior, Master: the badge adds a star, then a wreath.

entries.name: Service stripes and overseas service
entries.summary: Sleeve marks that show length of service and time overseas. Each branch has its own rules.
facts: Army dress service stripe: one per three years of service
Overseas service bar: one per six months overseas
WWI overseas service chevron: one per six months overseas
entries.remember: Stripes count years, bars and chevrons count overseas time.

variants.label: Overseas service chevron
variants.note: One chevron per six months overseas. Color to verify.

variants.label: Service stripe
variants.note: One stripe per three years. Color per uniform to verify.

variants.label: Overseas service bar
variants.note: One bar per six months overseas. Color per uniform to verify.

entries.name: Ranger tab
entries.summary: Tab worn above the unit patch by Ranger School graduates.
facts: Worn above the unit shoulder patch
Earlier eras and colors still need to be added

variants.label: Ranger tab
variants.note: Colors still need to be checked.

entries.name: Airborne tab
entries.summary: Tab worn above the unit patch by airborne-qualified soldiers.
facts: Worn above the unit shoulder patch

entries.name: Oak leaf cluster
entries.summary: Bronze or silver twig of four oak leaves with three acorns, showing a second or later award.
facts: Rule: an oak leaf cluster or numeral is awarded for each succeeding award (para 1-22)
Used on second and later awards of decorations (except the Air Medal), the ARCAM, and unit awards
Size: 13/32 inch on the suspension ribbon, 5/16 inch on the ribbon bar and unit award
Silver equals five bronze; wear no more than four per ribbon, then add a second ribbon
Posthumous awards: the device is attached to the medal (para 1-24h)
entries.remember: Bronze is one. Silver is five. Max four per ribbon.
sources: AR 600-8-22, Military Awards, 19 Jan 2024, para 1-22, 6-3
Text read from the copy hosted at ri.ng.mil (Rhode Island National Guard)

entries.name: Numeral
entries.summary: Arabic numeral, 3/16 inch, starting with 2, showing second and later awards of certain medals and ribbons.
facts: Used on the Air Medal, Overseas Service Ribbon, NCO Professional Development Ribbon, Armed Forces Reserve Medal, Reserve Components Overseas Training Ribbon, and the MFO Medal
Size: 3/16 inch; numbering begins with 2
entries.remember: Starts at 2. The Air Medal uses numerals, not clusters.
sources: AR 600-8-22, Military Awards, 19 Jan 2024, para 6-4
Text read from the copy hosted at ri.ng.mil (Rhode Island National Guard)

entries.name: V device
entries.summary: Bronze block letter V, 1/4 inch high, worn to show acts of heroism involving conflict with an armed enemy.
facts: Serifs at the top of either side of the V
Only one V is worn on the service ribbon, even for multiple valor awards
Use for any other purpose is prohibited
Not authorized on the Medal of Honor, DSC, Silver Star, or Soldier's Medal
entries.remember: V is for valor. One per ribbon.
sources: AR 600-8-22, Military Awards, 19 Jan 2024, para 6-5, table 3-1
Text read from the copy hosted at ri.ng.mil (Rhode Island National Guard)

entries.name: C device
entries.summary: Letter C worn to show meritorious service or achievement under combat conditions while personally exposed to risk.
facts: Authorized on the DSM, LM, DFC, Air Medal, ARCOM, and AAM on or after 7 January 2016
Not authorized on the Bronze Star Medal or the Meritorious Service Medal
Only one C is worn on the service ribbon
entries.remember: C is for combat, since 7 Jan 2016.
sources: AR 600-8-22, Military Awards, 19 Jan 2024, para 6-6

entries.name: R device
entries.summary: Letter R worn on decorations awarded for specific meritorious achievement.
facts: Authorized on the LM, MSM, ARCOM, and AAM on or after 7 January 2016
Not used on sustained-service medals
Only one R is worn on the service ribbon
entries.remember: R is for a specific achievement.
sources: AR 600-8-22, Military Awards, 19 Jan 2024, para 6-7

entries.name: M device
entries.summary: Letter M for Reserve Component members who volunteer for or serve on active duty in designated operations.
facts: Worn on the Armed Forces Reserve Medal
One per operation; numbering begins with the second award

entries.name: Clasps
entries.summary: Bars worn on suspension ribbons of certain medals.
facts: Used on the Army Good Conduct Medal, WWI Victory Medal, American Defense Service Medal, Army of Occupation Medal, and Antarctica Service Medal
Bronze bars, except the Good Conduct clasp

entries.name: Service star
entries.summary: Bronze or silver five-pointed star, 3/16 inch, showing participation in a named campaign or an additional award.
facts: On medals it marks a campaign; on ribbons it marks an additional award
A silver star is worn instead of five bronze stars
Also authorized on the Army Sea Duty Ribbon
entries.remember: Bronze is one. Silver is five.
